title: How can you find five numbers between two big numbers?
description: Meera's bus passes distance boards on a highway. The video writes five numbers between the first and the last board by changing the hundreds and the thousands.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number between is bigger than the first and smaller than the last; check both ends. Watch for a number with the right thousands that is smaller than the first end.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 1, numbers between
video_script.why: The child can name numbers between two close numbers but not yet between numbers with different thousands.
video_script.substitution: Pick numbers just after the first end with the same thousands, then numbers with the next thousand that stay below the last end, and check both ends.
video_script.anchor: Meera's bus passing distance boards on a highway
video_script.wrong_answer: twenty-three thousand, five hundred and fifty
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu picks twenty-three thousand, five hundred and fifty because the thousands are right. It is smaller than twenty-three thousand, five hundred and sixty-eight, so it is not between.
video_script.payoff_line: these five numbers all lie between the two boards

final_answer.spoken: twenty-three thousand six hundred, twenty-three thousand seven hundred and fifty, twenty-three thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine, twenty-four thousand and twenty-four thousand one hundred

never_show: a number below 23,568 marked as right
maths_rules: first board 23,568 and last board 24,234; both have five digits and start with 2; the thousands are 23 and 24
slip: 23,550 < 23,568, so it is not between them
24,000 and 24,100 are bigger than 23,568 and smaller than 24,234
video_script.design: Exercise: five numbers between two. Hint: look at the thousands, then compare with both ends. The highway with two boards stays on the stage and the line fills with the new boards.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='bus'/>Meera's bus runs along a highway with distance boards. The first board shows twenty-three thousand, five hundred and sixty-eight metres.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last board shows twenty-four thousand, two hundred and thirty-four metres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write five numbers for new boards between the first board and the last.

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Look at the thousands first. The first board has twenty-three thousand, and the last has twenty-four thousand.
<bookmark mark='need'/>A number between must be bigger than the first board and smaller than the last.
<bookmark mark='try'/>You can use twenty-three thousand or twenty-four thousand in front. Try again with this.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Twenty-three thousand, five hundred and fifty has the right thousands, so it fits.
<bookmark mark='low'/>It is smaller than twenty-three thousand, five hundred and sixty-eight.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Right thousands are not enough. Check the hundreds and tens too.

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Start right after the first board, with twenty-three thousand in front.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Twenty-three thousand, six hundred is bigger than the first board.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Twenty-three thousand, seven hundred and fifty is bigger too.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Twenty-three thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine is bigger as well, and still below twenty-four thousand.

beats.on_screen: 24,000 and 24,100 are placed on the line; the answer card shows 23,600, 23,750, 23,999, 24,000, 24,100
narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Next, take twenty-four thousand in front.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Twenty-four thousand is bigger than the first board and smaller than the last.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>Twenty-four thousand, one hundred is smaller than the last board too.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>These five numbers all lie between the two boards, and many other answers are right.
